title: PCA by power iteration

wrong.no_normalise.py: does not renormalise inside the loop (the vector overflows)
wrong.no_deflation.py: top_k_eigs never deflates, so every eigenpair is the same
wrong.deflate_without_lambda.py: deflates with v v^T instead of lambda v v^T
wrong.ones_start.py: starts from the all-ones vector, which can be orthogonal to the top eigenvector
wrong.eigenvalue_is_norm.py: eigenvalue is ||A v|| / ||v|| rather than the Rayleigh quotient v A v (differs before convergence)

hints: One iteration: v <- A @ v, then v <- v / norm(v). Repeating this pulls v towards the eigenvector with the largest eigenvalue.
The eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient v @ A @ v for the final unit vector. Start from a random vector (np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=d)), not the all-ones vector.
To get the next eigenpair, subtract what you found: A - lam * outer(v, v). pca_power is top_k_eigs on the covariance matrix of the centred data (divide by n - 1).
